items.title: 特朗普訪華之際 美國封堵中國公司在東南亞租用AI算力的「後門」

items.title: Delaware hit by rare November tornado
items.desc: Meanwhile, severe thunderstorms bring hailstones the size of baseballs in ArgentinaThe National Weather Service in the US has confirmed that an EF1 tornado touched down south-east of Newark in the Salem Woods neighbourhood, Delaware, on Thursday. The tornado reached 160 metres wide, had a path length of 4.4 miles (7.1km) and reached estimated peak winds of up to 100mph (161km/h). There were no injuries or fatalities but windows and roofs were damaged on several homes, a large hotel sign fell on to a number of cars, and a semi truck overturned on I95. Although Delaware often experiences a few tornadoes every year, this is only the second time the state has had tornado activity in November since 1950, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. The only other November tornado recorded was in 1989.Severe storms have also resulted in tornadoes in Argentina as well as large hailstones. A round of severe thunderstorms moved through the central Córdoba province on Friday, bringing hailstones up to the size of a baseball (about 7.5cm in diameter). Parts of the province recorded up to 73mm of rainfall in just six hours early on Saturday. Such storms are common at this time of year. Water vapour from the Amazon meeting the Andes quickly condenses, resulting in massive cloud formations often associated with heavy downpours, lightning, tornadoes and large hailstones. items.title: US officially loses measles-free status after 26 years in historic setback
items.desc: A major health organisation declared measles endemic in US for first time since 2000, reversing decades of progress.

items.title: Authorities take over Turkey's last pro-opposition broadcaster Sozcu TV
items.desc: Police raided the Istanbul headquarters of Sozcu TV on Tuesday, dealing another significant blow to Turkey's pro-opposition media. This is the third such seizure of pro-opposition media in just over a year. It comes amid public uproar over a multi-billion investment fund scandal that has affected the savings of nearly half a million people and piled pressure on President Recep Tayyip Erdogan's ruling AKP party ahead of elections in 2028. FRANCE 24's Jasper Mortimer reports from Ankara.

items.title: The centre cannot hold? Splintered moderates lag in French presidential race
items.desc: Five months to go before the French vote in the presidential election first round to choose Emmanuel Macron’s successor. Not much of a race so far for the top two spots and the May Second runoff: there’s the far-right’s Marine Le Pen, the far-left’s Jean-Luc Mélenchon and way behind there’s the rest. Whether on social media or in the streets, their supporters rule. A radical break with the mainstream.

items.title: France: Protesters march for better salaries across the country
items.desc: Tens of thousands of people took part in protests across France on Tuesday after unions called a new nationwide public sector strike to demand pay rises. What started over two months ago as high school student protests has now morphed into a wider movement against the increasing cost of living.

items.title: 'A lot of anger and a weak government': Why are French public sector workers striking?
items.desc: Tens of thousands of people took part in protests across France on Tuesday after unions called a new nationwide public sector strike to demand pay rises. It follows more than a month of unrest and often violent protests led by students that the government has failed to quell. France 24's Marc Perelman explains.

items.title: Deutsche Bank leaks: German lender's dealings with Russian oligarchs under scrutiny
items.desc: Germany's finance minister Tuesday urged "full transparency" from Deutsche Bank after international media outlets published reports based on millions of leaked documents that shine a light on questionable past business practices at the banking giant. They include ties to Russian oligarchs, the convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, and Donald Trump before he became US president. France 24's Douglas Herbert takes a closer look.

items.title: Latest cost-of-living protests bring more than 140,000 onto the streets across France
items.desc: Tens of thousands of people took part in protests across France on Tuesday after unions called a new nationwide public sector strike to demand pay rises. Participation was lower compared to previous demonstrations, with 146,000 people demonstrating across the country, according to the interior ministry, compared with 575,000 for the previous unified protests. Unions put Tuesday's number at 550,000.

items.title: Organisers hoping for 'joyful' demonstration as French public workers strike
items.desc: France braced for another day of protests Tuesday as unions called for a nationwide strike by public sector workers in a bid to secure pay rises. Hoping to avoid the violence that has marred recent protests in the country, organisers were hoping for a "joyous and festive" occasion, reports France 24's Claire Paccalin from a march in Paris.

items.title: Shenzhen: Inside ‘China’s Silicon Valley’
items.desc: When Xi Jinping hosts Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin at this year's APEC summit, he'll be doing it in one of his country's most technologically advanced cities. Shenzhen is China's premier hub for cutting-edge tech – a place where robo-taxis and AI-powered drones are a normal part of the background... Its current status is the result of decades of policies aimed at opening up the once communist country to international markets and foreign investment.

items.title: Deutsche Bank shares drop after reports exposing Epstein payments, Russia dealings
items.desc: Deutsche Bank shares fell more than 6% Tuesday after media reports based on leaked documents detailed the bank's dealings with clients including Russian oligarchs, US President Donald Trump and the late financier Jeffrey Epstein.

items.title: Serbia's student-backed MPs take seats in parliament after election win
items.desc: Serbia's Student ⁠List lawmakers entered parliament ​on Tuesday, cheered on by hundreds of supporters, after their October ​election victory ended 14 years of rule by the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS). The Student List, a group that includes academics, professionals, farmers, actors and activists ​chosen ‌by student assemblies, secured 140 seats in the ⁠250-member parliament in October 25 polls, while the SNS gained 104.

items.title: Trump says he takes possible Iran bomb threat to Washington 'very seriously'
items.desc: President Donald Trump said Tuesday that US authorities take any possible threats to Washington ‘very seriously’, following reports that Iran was planning to target senior Trump administration officials, possibly with a radioactive bomb.  Tehran dismissed the reports as ‘fabricated’.

items.title: Urban Zulu and '100 Reasons to Stay Single in Lagos': Telling African stories on their own terms
items.desc: Africa's creative industries are attracting growing international attention, from fashion and film to television and music. But as African stories reach audiences around the world, a bigger question is emerging: who gets to tell those stories, and who gets to shape how the continent is seen? At FAME Week Africa in Cape Town, arts24 met some of the creatives driving that conversation.

items.title: France's Le Pen promises to lower retirement age if she wins election
items.desc: French far-right ​leader Marine Le ​Pen vowed on Tuesday to repeal President ​Emmanuel ‌Macron's pension ⁠reform if she is ‌elected next spring and ⁠bring down the retirement age to ​60 to 62. She ‌also set out plans to ‌create a fund worth €900 ​billion ($990.54 billion) to help pay for pensions in ​the long term. It ​would take a generation ​to build up the fund, she added.

items.title: France hit by fresh nationwide public sector strike
items.desc: Demonstrators gathered across France on Tuesday after unions called a nationwide strike by public sector workers in a bid to secure pay rises, despite government efforts to ease tensions as demonstrations roil the country.

items.title: Calls for cooperation as ASEAN summit awaits Trump
items.desc: The twice-yearly ASEAN summit of Southeast Asian nations is underway, with major global powers also descending upon the Philippines. It is a crucial moment for the region, as ASEAN leaders look to strengthen their influence and collaboration in an increasingly divided global landscape. The arrival of US President Donald Trump on Tuesday is also being welcomed as well as protested, as Charli James reports.

items.title: Estonia closes its border with Russia but can it keep Moscow out?
items.desc: Estonia announced this weekend it would close its border with Russia, after blaming its eastern neighbour of attempting to sabotage one of its drone factories. But at a time when the internet has become one of Russia’s most potent weapons to wage hybrid warfare, does closing the border even matter?

items.title: 'We're kind of at a stalemate': French government and unions 'dancing around each other'
items.desc: Amid continuing protests in France and tense negotiations between the government and trade unions, Delano D'Souza is pleased to welcome Paul Smith, Associate Professor in French and Francophone Studies at the University of Nottingham. “What's happening is that there are two parties kind of dancing around each other.” Smith explains that the government wants to delay negotiations until after trade union elections on 10 December, while the unions want an agreement as quickly as possible. With talks “more or less broken down” over a two-point difference in public sector pay proposals, he describes the situation as “kind of at a stalemate.”

items.title: Did the US use ‘blackout bombs’ in Iran? Images reveal mysterious fibres at infrastructure sites
items.desc: Photographs published by Iranian local media suggest that US forces may have used graphite bombs, also known as ‘blackout bombs’, against infrastructure in Iran in recent days. These weapons are designed to disrupt electricity supplies by causing short circuits rather than physically destroying power facilities.

items.title: French far-right candidate Le Pen vows to end Macron's pension reform if elected
items.desc: Far-right French presidential contender Marine Le Pen said Tuesday she would eliminate President Emmanuel Macron's pension reform, allowing hundreds of thousands of French workers to retire earlier, and create a new €900 billion retirement fund. The frontrunner in polls to win the presidential race is seeking to convince investors she can balance one of her most popular pledges with promises ​to restore order to ‌the public finances.

items.title: Singer-songwriter Mélissa Laveaux: 'Women need more positions of power in the music industry'
items.desc: One of France's top musical artists has spoken to FRANCE 24 about the need to empower more women in music. Mélissa Laveaux is currently taking part in the "Les Femmes s'en mêlent" or "Women get involved" festival, which is holding a series of events across the country in an initiative that started nearly 30 years ago and is still going today. The aim is to address the underrepresentation of female artists at music festivals. She spoke to us in Perspective.

items.title: Ukraine: Two bridges in Kyiv heavily damaged by Russian strikes
items.desc: Russia hit two major bridges in Kyiv while Ukraine struck Moscow's link to annexed Crimea for the second night in a row, officials said Tuesday, ahead of a historic meeting of Chinese, US and Russian leaders. Detals from the ground by FRANCE 24 correspondent in Kyiv, Gulliver Cragg.

items.title: Ukraine strikes major Russian bridge in Crimea with drones and missiles
items.desc: Ukrainian drones and missiles struck a vital bridge linking Russia to the occupied Crimean Peninsula, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Tuesday, calling it an “unprecedented” operation as Russia reported that its forces downed a record number of Ukrainian drones for the second straight day. Meanwhile, Russia struck two major bridges in Kyiv.

items.title: Ukraine, Russia hit key bridges ahead of Putin-Xi
items.desc: Ukraine struck Russia's Crimean bridge for the second night in a row on Tuesday, shutting it down, while Russia hit two major bridges in Kyiv -- the latest wave of attacks that come ahead of a historic meeting of the Chinese, US and Russian leaders.

items.title: Two Marseille drug traffickers sentenced to life in prison over triple murder
items.desc: Two figures in Marseille’s drug trafficking ring were sentenced to life in prison on Monday over a triple murder committed in 2020. Among the victims was Brahim Chabane, the older brother of anti-drug activist and deputy mayor of Marseille Amine Kessaci.

items.title: 世卫组织：刚果（金）埃博拉疫情已致逾5400人死亡

items.title: 联合国报告：干扰内分泌化学物质可能在出生前影响人体健康

items.title: 世卫组织警告：检测和治疗不足使耐药感染患者面临风险
items.desc: 世界卫生组织周一发布的最新数据显示，尽管越来越多国家制定了应对抗微生物药物耐药性的计划，但检测和治疗服务仍存在明显不足，使许多患者继续面临风险。

items.title: 人工智能在回答气候科学问题时基本准确，但质疑会让其改变说法以迎合提问者
items.desc: 人工智能能够正确回答大多数气候科学问题。但最新研究表明，人们对人工智能所怀有的这种信心不一定完全可靠。
